sections.h2: Who is selling homes in Haverford Township, PA?
sections.html:
Haverford Township is a settled, high-value inner suburb on Philadelphia's western edge, and owners live in most of its homes. The 2025 Census estimate is 50,997 people, and 92.9 percent of them were in the same house a year before the survey.

The 2020 to 2024 survey shows 87.4 percent of homes owner-occupied, a typical value of $466,400 and rent near $1,766. Households earned a median $131,674, 64.4 percent of adults have a four-year degree, and 19.2 percent of residents are past 65. Long-held homes and older owners explain why so many Haverford sales follow a downsize, an inheritance or a house that has outlived its last update.

When a house needs a roof, kitchen or electrical work, the cost of making it market-ready is large at these price levels. Many owners set that against an as-is sale.

sections.h2: Where is Haverford Township and what are its neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Haverford Township fills the northeast corner of Delaware County, a 10-square-mile area that is all land. William Penn laid it out as part of the Welsh Tract, the first families arrived in 1682, and the township was incorporated in 1911. It is a first-class township run by a Board of Commissioners divided into wards.

Neighboring municipalities are Lower Merion Township to the northeast, the City of Philadelphia to the east, Upper Darby and Springfield townships to the south, Marple Township to the west and Radnor Township to the northwest. Cobbs Creek and Darby Creek mark parts of its boundary, and Naylors Run and Meadowbrook Run cross it.

  • Planned suburbs along the rail lines include Llanerch (1897) and Brookline (1909). Most of the large housing tracts date from after World War II, including Chatham Park.
  • Neighborhood names include Beechwood, Oakmont, Manoa, Westgate Hills, Paddock Farms, Merwood and Bon Air.
  • Parts of the Haverford, Ardmore, Wynnewood and Bryn Mawr communities lie inside the township.
  • Many of the post-war tracts share the Havertown postal address.

Name the neighborhood on your listing or offer request, because buyers search by it.

sections.h2: How do roads and SEPTA shape a Haverford house sale?
sections.html:
Good transit is one of the township's selling points. SEPTA's Norristown High Speed Line stops at seven stations inside the township, more than in any other township along the route: Township Line Road, Penfield, Beechwood-Brookline, Wynnewood Road, Ardmore Junction, Ardmore Avenue and Haverford. Suburban bus routes 103, 104, 105, 110, 112, 115, 120, 123 and 126 also serve the township and connect to the 69th Street Transportation Center.

As of 2018 the township had 158.26 miles of public roads, of which 123.78 miles are township-maintained and 34.48 miles belong to PennDOT. The I-476 Blue Route runs along the western edge, U.S. 1 follows Township Line Road, U.S. 30 crosses the northern tip on Lancaster Avenue, and Route 3 follows West Chester Pike. The mean commute for residents is 27.0 minutes.

sections.h2: Which schools and parks come with a Haverford address?
sections.html:
Public school students attend the School District of Haverford Township, which runs Chatham Park, Chestnutwold, Coopertown, Lynnewood and Manoa elementary schools for kindergarten through fifth grade, Haverford Middle School for sixth through eighth and Haverford High School for ninth through twelfth. Haverford College, an undergraduate liberal arts school founded by Welsh Quakers, is also in the area.

Golf shapes the local identity. Merion Golf Club hosted the U.S. Open in 1934, 1950, 1971, 1981 and 2013, and Llanerch Country Club hosted the 1958 PGA Championship. Neither affects your closing, but buyers often mention them when they describe why they want the area.

sections.h2: What does the township require when a Haverford house is a rental?
sections.html:
The Building and Codes Department licenses rentals every year and inspects them before a tenant moves in. Each time occupancy changes, the unit must be inspected again, so a buyer taking over a rented Haverford house should expect that step.

Haverford Township rental housing license, from the Building and Codes Department page
ItemRule
License fee$75 per dwelling unit
License periodMarch 1 to February 28 or 29
Due dateOn or before March 1
Late penalty$50, making $125 in total
Inspection or reinspection$50 per unit
Missed scheduled inspection$50
  • No more than three unrelated people may live in a rental house.
  • An owner-occupied unit may have only one roomer or boarder.
  • Student housing is allowed only as a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board.
  • Renting is a business activity for the township's Business Privilege Tax, so a landlord also files a business tax return.

The license application needs a list of occupants and a copy of the signed lease. If you are selling a rental, hand the buyer your current license and inspection records.

sections.h2: Which township permits should a Haverford seller check?
sections.html:
Contractors working in the township must hold a township license, and the department will not accept a permit application without a signed contract, proof of insurance with workers compensation and the cost estimate. Residential additions also need a plot plan with building coverage and impervious surface figures.

Online applications are accepted for plumbing, generator, mechanical, electrical, roofing and siding, fences, sheds, rental housing licenses and contractor licenses. If an earlier owner skipped a permit for a deck or addition, ask the department what its records show before you list.

Trees are regulated too. A permit is required to plant, prune, remove or spray a public shade tree, and owners must keep private branches 12 feet above public walks and 14 feet above streets.

The department also lists a contact for use and occupancy (U&O) inspections. Find out whether one applies to your sale, and what it costs, before you fix a closing date.

sections.h2: How are transfer tax and recording handled in Delaware County?
sections.html:
A deed for a Haverford Township property is filed with the Delaware County Recorder of Deeds. The state sets a 1 percent transfer tax on the property's value, and the recorder collects a local share that is split among school districts and municipalities.

Inherited property is exempt when it passes to heirs, which matters if you received the house and now plan to sell. The revenue department's Delaware County valuation factor is 1.83 for deeds accepted during the year that began July 1, 2026. Your title company can tell you the combined percentage and who pays which part.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Haverford Township house?
sections.html:
Owners here tend to pick one of three routes.

  • An agent listing can fetch the strongest price for a well-kept house, with showings and repair requests along the way.
  • Selling yourself avoids a commission and puts pricing and paperwork on your desk.
  • A cash offer takes the house in its present state, useful when you are clearing an estate or the property needs major work.

At Haverford price levels the gap between an as-is offer and a renovated sale can be wide, so work out what you keep on each path.

faqs.q: Must a Haverford rental be inspected before sale?
faqs.a: The township inspects before a tenant moves in and again whenever occupancy changes, at $50 per unit. Keep your latest rental license and inspection record ready, and expect the buyer to plan for the next inspection.

faqs.q: Is an inherited Haverford house taxed on transfer?
faqs.a: State rules exempt property inherited with or without a will. Your later sale to a buyer is a new transfer and carries the state 1 percent plus any local share.

faqs.q: How many unrelated people can share a Haverford rental?
faqs.a: The township's rental license rules cap a rental house at three unrelated residents. Student housing needs a special exception from the Zoning Hearing Board.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed to take down a tree before selling in Haverford?
faqs.a: Township code requires a permit to plant, prune, remove or spray a public shade tree, meaning one on public property or a street. Trees on private land follow different rules, so call the Building and Codes Department if unsure.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Haverford Township addresses?
faqs.a: The School District of Haverford Township does. It runs five elementary schools, one middle school and one high school, so name the elementary zone when you describe the house.
